applies_why: The judge text issues an UNDERDETERMINED verdict on an Acts 2:30 row, so K-S2's limits on grounds for that verdict apply.
quote: D5 vs C1 (Acts 2:30): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] and [CR3] answered the loins/seed row with Genesis 46:26 and Hebrews 7:10 (loins at depth) and the legal/flesh distinction, while [DR3] presses that the only named Davidic man is Joseph; neither chain forces the other.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: Phrase: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED. Reading 1: it forbids only an explicit single-verse-silence ground. Reading 2: it also forbids any UNDERDETERMINED finding where the row's verse leaves competing chains unresolved.
why: The judge's stated reason is that two chains do not force each other, not that a single verse fails to state the link or its contrary, so K-S2 is not breached.
